    Diffusive and dispersive properties of the tracer advection schemes¶

    Aim of Tutorial¶

    The aim of this tutorial is to give the readers an opportunity to run the salt block simulation using the different advection schemes. Here we choose to use the transport of a block of salt to demonstrate how the diffusive and dispersive properties of the advection scheme impact the outcome of a simulation.

    To run the simulations in this demonstrator you must have followed Tutorial 1 beforehand.

    Dispersive scheme¶

    An example of a dispersive scheme in NEMO 5.0 is the CENtred advection scheme (CEN).

    In a dispersive scheme the different components of the signal travel at different speeds which can generate side-lobes.

    To see more explanations on dispersive schemes¶

    Diffusive scheme¶

    An example of a diffusive scheme in NEMO 5.0 is the Upstream Biased Scheme (UBS).

    A diffusive scheme causes sharp edges and slopes in signals to flatten. The UBS scheme is a diffusive scheme coupled with a 4th order dispersive scheme (CEN4), therefore it can generate side-lobes which the diffusion helps to tame.

    To see more explanations on diffusive schemes¶

    Corrected scheme¶

    An example of a corrected scheme in NEMO 5.0 is the Flux Corrected Transport scheme (FCT).

    The FCT scheme is initially a dispersive scheme to which is combined a limiter function to correct the side-lobes generated.

    Phase speed and damping effect¶

    To see more explanations on phase speed and damping effect¶

    In [121]:
    Copied! 
    dx = 10000 #[m]
dt = 2*3600 #[s]
c0 = 0.5 #[m/s]
theta_max = min(np.pi, np.pi*dx/(c0*dt)) #maximum value of theta to avoid spectral aliasing
k_max = theta_max/dx

def phase_speed(f, dx, dt):
    """f[t, x] -> k, c(k) mesuré par la rotation de phase entre pas de temps."""
    F = np.fft.rfft(f - f.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True), axis=1)
    k = 2*np.pi*np.fft.rfftfreq(f.shape[1], dx)
    dphi = np.angle(F[1:] / F[:-1])# = -ω dt with numpy convention 
    w = np.abs(F[1:] * F[:-1]) # amplitude weighting
    c = np.full(k.shape, np.nan)
    D = np.full(k.shape, np.nan)
    A = np.abs(F[1:] / F[:-1]) 
    for i in range(1, len(k)):
        c[i] = -np.sum(w[:, i] * dphi[:, i]) / (np.sum(w[:, i]) * k[i] * dt)
        D[i] = np.sum(w[:,i]*A[:,i]) / np.sum(w[:,i])
    return k, c, D

theta = np.linspace(1e-3, theta_max, 400)                       # θ = k·dx
theory_cp  = { #theoretical expression of c_p = ω/k for CEN2 and CEN4 for spatial discretisation only
    'cen2': np.sin(theta) / theta, 
    'cen4': (4/3*np.sin(theta) - 1/6*np.sin(2*theta)) / theta}
theory_D = { #theoretical expression of damping for UBS for spatial discretisation only
    'ubs': np.exp(-c0*dt/(3*dx)*(1-np.cos(theta))**2), 
}

# Secondary X-axis to show the wavelength scale
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))
ax2 = ax.twiny()


for name, f in soce.items():
    k, c, D = phase_speed(f, dx, dt)
    k=k[ k < k_max]
    c = c[:len(k)]
    ax.plot(k*dx, c / c0, '.', color=colors[name], label=f'{name} (measured on NEMO)')
    wavelength = 2*np.pi/k[1:]/1000
    ax2.plot(wavelength, c[1:] / c0, '.',  alpha = 0, label=f'{name} (measured on NEMO)')
    plt.gca().invert_xaxis() 

    

for name, c_th in theory_cp.items():
    ax.plot(theta, c_th, '--', label=f'{name} (theory, spatial only)')
    
ax.axhline(1, color='k', lw=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel(r'$k\,\Delta x$')
ax2.set_xlabel('wavelength [km]', color='r')
ax.set_ylabel(r'$c_{num}/c_0$')
ax.set_title(r'Phase speed')
ax.legend()
plt.show()



# Secondary X-axis to show the wavelength scale
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))
ax2 = ax.twiny()

for name, f in soce.items():
    k, c, D = phase_speed(f, dx, dt)
    k=k[ k < k_max]
    D = D[:len(k)]
    ax.plot(k*dx, D, '.', color=colors[name], label=f'{name} (measured on NEMO)')
    wavelength = 2*np.pi/k[1:]/1000
    ax2.plot(wavelength, c[1:] / c0, '.',  alpha = 0, label=f'{name} (measured on NEMO)')
    plt.gca().invert_xaxis() 
    
for name, D_th in theory_D.items():
    ax.plot(theta, D_th, '--',label=f'{name} (theory, spatial only)')
    
ax.axhline(1, color='k', lw=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel(r'$k\,\Delta x$')
ax2.set_xlabel('wavelength [km]', color='r')
ax.set_ylabel(r'$D$')
ax.set_title(r'Damping factor')
ax.set_ylim(D_th.min()*0.9, 1.1)
ax.legend()

plt.tight_layout()

    dx = 10000 #[m] dt = 2*3600 #[s] c0 = 0.5 #[m/s] theta_max = min(np.pi, np.pi*dx/(c0*dt)) #maximum value of theta to avoid spectral aliasing k_max = theta_max/dx def phase_speed(f, dx, dt): """f[t, x] -> k, c(k) mesuré par la rotation de phase entre pas de temps.""" F = np.fft.rfft(f - f.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True), axis=1) k = 2*np.pi*np.fft.rfftfreq(f.shape[1], dx) dphi = np.angle(F[1:] / F[:-1])# = -ω dt with numpy convention w = np.abs(F[1:] * F[:-1]) # amplitude weighting c = np.full(k.shape, np.nan) D = np.full(k.shape, np.nan) A = np.abs(F[1:] / F[:-1]) for i in range(1, len(k)): c[i] = -np.sum(w[:, i] * dphi[:, i]) / (np.sum(w[:, i]) * k[i] * dt) D[i] = np.sum(w[:,i]*A[:,i]) / np.sum(w[:,i]) return k, c, D theta = np.linspace(1e-3, theta_max, 400) # θ = k·dx theory_cp = { #theoretical expression of c_p = ω/k for CEN2 and CEN4 for spatial discretisation only 'cen2': np.sin(theta) / theta, 'cen4': (4/3*np.sin(theta) - 1/6*np.sin(2*theta)) / theta} theory_D = { #theoretical expression of damping for UBS for spatial discretisation only 'ubs': np.exp(-c0*dt/(3*dx)*(1-np.cos(theta))**2), } # Secondary X-axis to show the wavelength scale fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5)) ax2 = ax.twiny() for name, f in soce.items(): k, c, D = phase_speed(f, dx, dt) k=k[ k < k_max] c = c[:len(k)] ax.plot(k*dx, c / c0, '.', color=colors[name], label=f'{name} (measured on NEMO)') wavelength = 2*np.pi/k[1:]/1000 ax2.plot(wavelength, c[1:] / c0, '.', alpha = 0, label=f'{name} (measured on NEMO)') plt.gca().invert_xaxis() for name, c_th in theory_cp.items(): ax.plot(theta, c_th, '--', label=f'{name} (theory, spatial only)') ax.axhline(1, color='k', lw=0.8) ax.set_xlabel(r'$k\,\Delta x$') ax2.set_xlabel('wavelength [km]', color='r') ax.set_ylabel(r'$c_{num}/c_0$') ax.set_title(r'Phase speed') ax.legend() plt.show() # Secondary X-axis to show the wavelength scale fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5)) ax2 = ax.twiny() for name, f in soce.items(): k, c, D = phase_speed(f, dx, dt) k=k[ k < k_max] D = D[:len(k)] ax.plot(k*dx, D, '.', color=colors[name], label=f'{name} (measured on NEMO)') wavelength = 2*np.pi/k[1:]/1000 ax2.plot(wavelength, c[1:] / c0, '.', alpha = 0, label=f'{name} (measured on NEMO)') plt.gca().invert_xaxis() for name, D_th in theory_D.items(): ax.plot(theta, D_th, '--',label=f'{name} (theory, spatial only)') ax.axhline(1, color='k', lw=0.8) ax.set_xlabel(r'$k\,\Delta x$') ax2.set_xlabel('wavelength [km]', color='r') ax.set_ylabel(r'$D$') ax.set_title(r'Damping factor') ax.set_ylim(D_th.min()*0.9, 1.1) ax.legend() plt.tight_layout() plt.show()

    The square-wave signal contains all wavelengths. We can analyse the speed at which each component of the signal travels (phase speed) and how much amplitude it loses (damping factor) for all wavelengths. To do so we exploit the fourier transform of the tracer field.

    Linear schemes (UBS & CEN) are compared to their theoretical curves. For non-linear schemes (FCT) theoretical curves cannot easily be deducted.

    Waves are always slower than \(c_0\), the more so the shorter they are. The phase error is of order 4 for UBS&CEN4 instead of order 2 for CEN2, therefore the CEN2 curve decreases more quickly than the UBS&CEN4 one.

    The dispersive schemes do not suffer from damping. The damping for UBS kills short waves while leaving long waves almost untouched. As high frequency components are responsible for sharp fronts in signal it explains why the signal is smoothed out.
